    tile_h = row_bounds[1] - row_bounds[0] - 1
    tile_w = col_bounds[1] - col_bounds[0] - 1

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])

    # Identify full separator rows and columns.
    row_seps = [r for r in range(h) if len(set(grid[r])) == 1]
    col_seps = [c for c in range(w) if all(grid[r][c] == grid[0][c] for r in range(h))
                and len({grid[r][c] for r in range(h)}) == 1]

    # The separator color is the color appearing throughout those lines.
    sep_colors = [grid[r][0] for r in row_seps] + [grid[0][c] for c in col_seps]
    sep_color = max(set(sep_colors), key=sep_colors.count)

    row_bounds = [-1] + row_seps + [h]
    col_bounds = [-1] + col_seps + [w]
    tiles = []
    for ri in range(len(row_bounds) - 1):
        r0, r1 = row_bounds[ri] + 1, row_bounds[ri + 1]
        for ci in range(len(col_bounds) - 1):
            c0, c1 = col_bounds[ci] + 1, col_bounds[ci + 1]
            tile = [row[c0:c1] for row in grid[r0:r1]]
            tiles.append((r0, c0, tile))

    # Choose the tile with the most non-background cells as the pattern.
    colors = [v for row in grid for v in row if v != sep_color]
    background = max(set(colors), key=colors.count)
    source = max(tiles, key=lambda item: sum(v != background for row in item[2] for v in row))[2]

    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    for r0, c0, _ in tiles:
        for r in range(len(source)):
            for c in range(len(source[0])):
                out[r0 + r][c0 + c] = source[r][c]
    return out
